fix_summary: G7-02 Independent Review correction: replaced the anonymous /api/auth/setup endpoint (which let any caller mint a signed cookie) with a PIN-validated /api/auth/login endpoint. The BFF now requires an operator-authenticated cookie carrying the op='operator' claim; cookies without this claim are rejected even if their signature is valid.

trust_boundary.design: POST /api/auth/login accepts {pin}, validates via constant-time comparison, issues an HMAC-signed HttpOnly+SameSite=Strict cookie with op='operator' + operatorId claims. The BFF proxy /api/genesis/* requires this cookie and rejects any cookie without the op claim.
residual_limitations: PIN is a shared secret. Anyone with the PIN can mint a BFF session. Suitable for controlled environments with operator-only network access; NOT for untrusted network exposure without additional layers (rate limiting, IP allow-listing, mTLS, OAuth).
Single-operator model: all BFF sessions share the single GENESIS_API_KEY's callerId. The cookie's operatorId field is for audit only — it does NOT provide multi-user isolation at the gateway level.
Cookies do NOT survive server restart unless GENESIS_BFF_SECRET is set (per-process random secret in dev). This is intentional for the controlled environment; production must set GENESIS_BFF_SECRET.

Cookies have an 8-hour TTL. After expiry, the user must re-authenticate. Logout (POST /api/auth/logout) clears the cookie client-side but does NOT revoke the server-side HMAC signature (stateless design).

PIN comparison uses Node.js timingSafeEqual (constant-time). The 401 INVALID_PIN response does not distinguish 'wrong PIN' from 'server misconfigured (no PIN set)' — both return 401 to avoid leaking server state.
Rate limiting is NOT implemented. An attacker could brute-force the PIN without throttling. Production hardening must add rate limiting (out of G7-02 scope).

implemented_features: G7-02 auth-gate fix: REMOVED /api/auth/setup (anonymous cookie minting endpoint). The endpoint now returns 404 (deleted route).

G7-02 auth-gate fix: ADDED POST /api/auth/login that requires a server-validated operator PIN (GENESIS_OPERATOR_PIN env var). Constant-time comparison via Node.js timingSafeEqual. On success, issues an HMAC-signed cookie with op='operator' + operatorId claims.
G7-02 auth-gate fix: ADDED POST /api/auth/logout that clears the cookie (Set-Cookie with Max-Age=0).

G7-02 auth-gate fix: cookie payload now includes op='operator' claim. The BFF /api/genesis/* proxy's authorize() function rejects any cookie that lacks this claim — even if the signature is otherwise valid. This is the CRITICAL correction: a signed cookie is no longer sufficient; it must also carry the operator claim, which only /api/auth/login can issue (after PIN validation).

G7-02 auth-gate fix: cookie payload now includes operatorId bound to the authenticated operator context. NOT multi-user isolation — all calls share the gateway's callerId via GENESIS_API_KEY. The operatorId is for audit logging only.
G7-02 auth-gate fix: cookie library exports verifyTokenWithSecret for unit testing (allows signing tokens with a known secret and verifying them without depending on the production SECRET).

G7-02 auth-gate fix: AuthGate component — PIN entry form shown when /api/genesis/health returns 401. Calls POST /api/auth/login, renders the app on 200, shows 'Invalid PIN' on 401, shows 'Server not configured' on 503.

G7-02 auth-gate fix: 14 adversarial E2E tests (anonymous caller attempts, login flow, tampered cookie, wrong secret, missing op claim, expired cookie, method whitelist, logout).

known_limitations: PIN-based auth is single-factor. Suitable for controlled environments with operator-only network access; NOT for untrusted network exposure without additional layers (rate limiting, IP allow-listing, mTLS, OAuth).
Single-operator model: all BFF sessions share the single GENESIS_API_KEY's callerId. The cookie's operatorId is for audit only — NOT multi-user isolation at the gateway level.
Cookies do NOT survive server restart unless GENESIS_BFF_SECRET is set (per-process random secret in dev). In production, GENESIS_BFF_SECRET MUST be set.
Cookies have an 8-hour TTL. After expiry, the user must re-authenticate via /api/auth/login.
PIN comparison is constant-time (timingSafeEqual). The 401 response does not distinguish 'wrong PIN' from 'server misconfigured' — both return 401 to avoid leaking server state.
Rate limiting is NOT implemented. Production hardening must add it before any non-local deployment.

GENESIS_OPERATOR_PIN defaults to 'dev-local-pin' in dev mode (when NODE_ENV != production and GENESIS_OPERATOR_PIN is unset). In production, GENESIS_OPERATOR_PIN MUST be set to a strong random value (>= 32 chars) or /api/auth/login returns 401 (fail-closed).

SameSite=Strict prevents the cookie from being sent on cross-site requests. If the UI is embedded in an iframe on a different origin, the cookie will not be sent — use SameSite=Lax + CSRF tokens instead (out of G7-02 scope).
